exposure: Non-pharmacological agents (Foley's catheter and membrane stripping)
Combined non-pharmacological and pharmacological agents (Foley's catheter and membrane stripping followed by oxytocin)
cohort: The study included 296 pregnant women admitted to the labor room for induction of labor, divided into three groups based on the induction method used.
finding: Non-pharmacological methods alone led to higher cesarean rates despite improved cervical status, while the combination of non-pharmacological and pharmacological agents resulted in higher normal delivery rates and fewer cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Combining non-pharmacological and pharmacological agents for labor induction resulted in higher normal delivery rates and a significantly lower cesarean section rate compared to either method used alone.
